product_target: Given a downstream driver and optional datasheet/reference upstream drivers, AURA can produce a bounded, observable, explainable, replayable, interruptible, reversible upstream-style conversion workflow with deterministic gates and PM oversight.
summary: AURA has strong deterministic verification/gating pieces and a proven WCD937x/WCD9378 learning loop, but generation, mode selection, compile/runtime gates, prompt reuse, and folder governance are not yet productized.

categories.assessment: Driver runs include allowed sources and evidence artifacts, but no single mandatory input package schema exists.
conversion_gate requires allowed_sources.json, but generation-time enforcement still depends on agent discipline.
Artifacts can record SHAs; baseline pinning is not enforced by a run manifest for every conversion.
Mode choice is currently PM/prompt judgment; no deterministic selector exists.
multifile_scoring and gate support converted dirs and file maps.
Gate can WARN when scoring is skipped, but no first-class new-driver mode or alternate score exists.
v3/v4 scoring and gate support existing upstream targets.
Verifier checks function coverage when lineage exists; schema quality varies by run.
conversion_verifier flags target/reference derivation and downstream reuse risk.
Plans and manual runs exist; canonical compile/checkpatch gates are not implemented.
Evidence requests/checklists exist for WCD9378, but no parser/gate consumes logs yet.
Hardware evidence requirements are documented, but acquisition and acceptance are manual.
PM behavior is strong in conversation but not yet packaged as an installed skill/policy.
Future terminals need AGENTS plus skill/runbook; conversation memory is currently important.
AURA, AURA_V1, AURA_V1_ops, and AURA_V1_upstream create source-of-truth ambiguity.
Prompts are not centrally versioned or discoverable as reusable templates.
This audit creates a draft skill; it is not installed globally yet.
